section.sectionSummaryBrief: Human service can elevate even the past, and Adam's service on Rosh Hashanah perfected all of creation retroactively.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter
(that Rosh Hashanah,
the day when the first man was created,
is the beginning of Your works)
in a deeper sense,
it is known that the service of man has the power to change even the past.
And from this it is understood
(all the more so)
regarding the service of the first man, who was the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He,
that the elevation he effected in all created beings through his proclamation, "Come, let us bow down... before Hashem our Maker," also applies to their existence prior to his service.
For since
the original intent of creation was that man, through his service, should draw down a revelation of G-dliness into the world,
therefore,
after a revelation of G-dliness is drawn into the world, an elevation is thereby effected also in the existence of the world that preceded it,
and especially since its purpose is the preparation for the revelation that is drawn down through the service of man.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The day of Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of all works, including the first five days of creation, because Adam's service elevated and renewed them.
section.t: And this is what [is meant by] the day of Rosh Hashanah,
the day when the first man was created,
is the beginning of Your works,
for the simple explanation
(and a matter does not depart from its simple meaning)
[is that] "the beginning of Your works" is the beginning of all the works,
even the works that were in the first five days of creation
(including also the time of those days),
for through the service of the first man, an elevation and renewal was effected also in the existence of the world that preceded this,
and therefore this day is the beginning of Your works,
the beginning of all of creation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as on the first Rosh Hashanah Adam's service perfected creation anew, so too each year Israel's coronation of Hashem perfects and renews all of creation, even above.
section.t: And just as on the first Rosh Hashanah,
on the day when the first man was created,
the perfection of creation was effected
(Your works),
and in a manner of renewal
(the beginning of Your works),
so too is it on Rosh Hashanah of every single year,
for through Israel crowning the Holy One, blessed be He, that He be King over them and over the entire world,
perfection and renewal are effected in all of creation,
and even to the extent that through this, perfection and renewal are effected also above,
according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov
and the Alter Rebbe
on the statement of the Mishnah,
"Know what is above from you,"
[meaning] that all the matters that are above are from you.
